messages:
aj: quick heads-up — after the head-dim scaling change rolled to canary, Llama-3 streaming p95 jumped ~70ms. p50 unchanged. noticed on a small subset (region eu-west).

sasha: can you paste the numbers and the canary id?

aj: canary id `canary-2028-05-03-3`
aj: p50 18ms -> 18ms, p90 42ms -> 43ms, p95 76ms -> 148ms (after change). reproducible with a 4-token prompt streaming to client.

runtime-bot: deploy canary-2028-05-03-3 completed on pool:redwood-eu-3 (tags: head-scale-v2).

maria: interesting — head-dim packing often causes a hidden copy for odd multiples. we changed head_dim mapping from 64-> 80 for L2->L3 variants, that flips the GEMM kernel selection for the QKV path. if the kernel selector picks a fallback (non-vectorized) path, token latency spikes on streaming because KV insert/evict is serial.

leo: repro steps i used (local canary):
```bash
# quick repro flow
python -m regen_client --model llama-3-canary --stream --prompt "Hi" --max_tokens 4
# env
export RW_POOL=redwood-eu-3
```
log snippet:
```
[2028-05-03T14:12:46Z] qkv_gemm: chosen_kernel=gemm_fallback_8x8
[2028-05-03T14:12:46Z] kv_insert: latency_ms=6.3
[2028-05-03T14:12:46Z] total_token_emit: delta_ms=120
```

sasha: so kernel selector fell back to 8x8 path. do we have perf profile to show where time went?

aj: yes — sampling profile attached (small excerpt):
```
cpu: 42% qkv_gemm::fallback8x8
      18% kv_cache::serialize
      12% token_emit::io_wait
      8% copy::aligned_memcpy
```

maria: that aligns with the hypothesis — fallback GEMM increases per-token compute and forces extra copies during prefix/KV handling. two quick mitigations: (1) widen kernel selector to prefer the 16x16 kernel for these head_dims (fast path), or (2) add a tiny packing shim that pads heads to 128-aligned buffers only for streaming codepath. (2) is lower-risk but adds cost.

leo: i can prototype the packing shim today. how disruptive is a selector tweak? any compatibility/quality risk?

sasha: selector tweak is fine but needs regression testing on other shapes (Mixtral/Mistral) — we saw different models invert kernel preference. also check quantized kernels: int8 kernels behave differently on head dims.

maria: also flag: rope_theta default changed in model config for some Llama-3 checkpoints. rope scaling alters positional index mapping which slightly shifts KV cache hit patterns for prefix caching heuristics. if rope_theta increases effective rotation range, our prefix cache stride and eviction heuristics may mis-predict and trigger more KV evictions in a mixed-batch scenario. not the main cause here, but worth checking.

aj: good call. @maria can you add a quick check to the profiler that dumps kernel choice + rope_theta + head_dim per request in canary? small CSV is fine.

maria: on it — will push a tiny change to runtime-observability (nonblocking) that emits `kernel,head_dim,rope_theta,chosen_kernel` for the next canary run.

runtime-bot: perf dashboard updated: https://perf.redwood-internal/pool/redwood-eu-3/canary-2028-05-03-3 (p95 chart annotated).

aj: action items:
- leo: prototype packing shim (ETA EOD)
- maria: add CSV emitter to canary (ETA 2h)
- sasha: run cross-model regression on selector changes (ETA tomorrow AM)
- aj: hold canary expansion until we have shim/selector patch or can confirm no regression on other models

leo: ack, starting now.

sasha: ack. will schedule test matrix (L2/ L3 / Mixtral / Qwen) across quantized and fp16 kernels.

aj: thanks — please post updates here. if we see >30ms p95 regressions in other regions, we revert the head-scale change. :thumbsup:

maria: one more note — streaming tail amplifies even small per-token deltas. for production fallback we should also consider a transient-mode: when kernel selector picks fallback and streaming p95 crosses threshold, route streaming requests to a compatible model variant (e.g., pinned head_dim multiple) until optimized kernel available. can file a follow-up RFC.

aj: agree. creating a short RFC after this is wrapped up. closing thread for now but will re-open with results. :white_check_mark:
